Users can now create fully licensed music, voiceovers, and sound effects on Adobe's Firefly AI assistant. Here's the full rundown.

Firefly audio tools officially open for use

Adobe recently partnered with Berklee College of Music on a survey examining the workflows and challenges faced by video creators, musicians, and marketers. Adobe says every respondent reported using music in their videos, with 32.7% using AI-generated music. 43.2% pointed to legal and copyright risks as the biggest barrier to using music, while 38.9% cited licensing costs.

Adobe today announced that the Generate Music tool is officially open for use on Firefly, alongside the launch of two other tools: Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects.

Generate Music creates original, fully licensed tracks tailored to your video's length and mood, letting you use the music on any platform without worrying about licensing or takedowns. Generate Speech converts scripts into clear, natural-sounding voiceovers—you can choose Adobe's in-house Firefly voice model or ElevenLabs' solution. Generate Sound Effects creates custom sounds to match on-screen action, timing, and energy.

The company stresses that Generate Music produces fully licensed music ready for finished work, and like Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects, requires no additional subscription to generate assets suitable for commercial use.

Generate Music can analyze video content and automatically build editable prompts based on what it deems most fitting. Users can also adjust parameters like tempo, energy, and length before hitting "generate" to receive four options.

With Generate Speech, users can add emotional expression and pronunciation markers to specific parts of the script, while Generate Sound Effects lets users enter text prompts or record audio as a reference for generating sound.

Here's what Adobe provided:

The new tools are now available on Adobe Firefly's desktop and mobile web apps.

Adobe expands AI model lineup within Firefly

Separately, Adobe also announced today that Gemini Omni Flash has landed on Firefly, letting users "combine video, audio, and image inputs with text to give you more ways to develop videos and reshape them through back-and-forth revisions…".

This move comes just days after the company added Runway Aleph 2.0 and Kling 2.0 to its third-party model toolkit, which already included models from Google, Kling AI, Luma AI, OpenAI, Runway, and Adobe itself.
